items.title: Battery demand 'straps on a rocket' as rooftop solar passes its peak
items.description: Even as Australia appears to have passed the peak of solar uptake, demand for batteries is seemingly headed into orbit.

items.title: Ferguson offered Epstein woman with 'great body' after his release from prison
items.description: Emails contained in the Epstein files show former British royal Sarah Ferguson told the convicted child sex offender she knew a "single" woman with a "great body" he should meet, weeks after his 2009 release from prison.

items.title: Adventurer's high praise for 13yo boy and his mum after miracle WA rescue
items.description: "Outback Mike" Atkinson says the Appelbee family's ability to stay calm and make smart decisions was critical to their survival after they were swept out to sea off Geographe Bay.

items.title: Breaking: Randa Abdel-Fattah to appear at Adelaide literary event in March
items.description: Palestinian Australian author, lawyer and activist Randa Abdel-Fattah will be appearing at the one-off literary event organised to fill the void left by the cancellation of this year's Adelaide Writers' Week, organisers have announced.

items.title: The government has options to fight inflation, but most are unpopular
items.description: The federal government has a variety of options available if it wants to do more to stave off inflation, but none are popular.

items.title: Why the 'Lucky Generation' without mortgages is still dismayed by RBA rate hike
items.description: A third of Australians could benefit if banks raise deposit rates on savings, while mortgage holders are having to decide what to cut back on.

items.title: Trump tells Republicans 'we should take over the voting'
items.description: Donald Trump says he wants Republicans to "nationalise" US elections and has encouraged his party to "take over the voting" in at least some parts of the country.

items.title: AI bots have created a religion, but experts say that's not the scary part
items.description: A social network run entirely by AI bots has attracted more than a million users — but experts warn it is not what the bots are saying that poses the true risk.

items.title: What the Epstein files tell us about Andrew's 'car crash' 2019 interview
items.description: Documents released last week have shed more light on what the former prince might have been lying about in that fateful sit-down with the BBC's flagship current affairs program, Newsnight.

items.title: Live: Tech sell-off drives Wall Street lower as bitcoin crashes below $US73,000
items.description: The Australian share market is likely to fall in morning trade after a brutal session on Wall Street, weighed down by massive losses in the share prices of tech and AI companies like Nvidia and Microsoft, while bitcoin has plunged to a 16-month low. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Chalmers downplays reports he's considering capital gains tax overhaul
items.description: Treasurer Jim Chalmers is downplaying reports he is considering a capital gains tax overhaul and that the government had "other priorities when it came to tax reform". Follow live.

items.title: No plans to increase security at Wittenoom after blogger's 'devastating' visit
items.description: Asbestos disease advocates criticise a Queensland blogger for taking her daughter to one of Australia's most contaminated sites.

items.title: One Nation, a popular premier and independents: SA Liberals face three major threats
items.description: While South Australia is considered a more moderate state than Queensland or New South Wales, March's state election will still be a chance to gauge the seriousness of One Nation's polling surge and the impact of the Coalition split on the Liberal Party's brand.

items.title: Jet fighter downs Iranian drone near US aircraft carrier
items.description: The US military has shot down an Iranian drone that was flying towards an American aircraft carrier in waters near Iran, US authorities say.

items.title: Sixth man charged over alleged Sydney-based 'satanic' paedophile ring
items.description: Another man has been charged and a further 145 alleged offenders have been referred to international law enforcement agencies as part of an investigation into a satanic child sex abuse material ring.

items.title: Reality bites for Brisbane 2032 as 'dispersed' Games costs escalate
items.description: Brisbane 2032 president Andrew Liveris says the bid budget "bears no resemblance to reality" as the financial impact of a dispersed Olympics hits home.

items.title: Quiz: You may be able to rock out on one, but do you know how guitars are made?
items.description: From shaping to tuning — how much do you know about how an acoustic guitar is made?

items.title: Structure lost in Deep Creek blaze as CFS battles wind changes
items.description: A bushfire on South Australia's Fleurieu Peninsula has now burnt more than 2,500 hectares, with the CFS saying it believes "at least one structure" has been lost in the blaze.

items.title: Missing bushwalker found alive in the Blue Mountains
items.description: Authorities have found 71-year-old David Elliot alive following a multi-agency search when he failed to return from a 30-kilometre walk.

items.title: Jill Biden's first husband charged with killing wife
items.description: William Stevenson is charged with the murder of his wife, Linda Stevenson, at their Delaware home on December 28.

items.title: Hero teen 'passed out' after open-ocean swim to save family
items.description: A WA mother says asking her teenage son to swim four kilometres through rough seas to get help after their family was swept out to sea, was "one of the hardest decisions" she has ever made.

items.title: Teenager slashed and run over in St Kilda incident
items.description: Two men described by police as acting like "rabid dogs" are on the run after allegedly slashing a teenager with a knife and running him over in an incident in Melbourne on Tuesday night.

items.title: 'I thought I was a bad parent': Thousands struggle with 'school can't'
items.description: Thousands of Australian parents are struggling with children who cannot go to school. A new podcast and e-book have been released to help support them.

items.title: Residents burnt out of 'paradise' determined to rebuild
items.description: The Cochrane family has called the Otways home for more than four decades. Even after fires destroyed their property, they do not plan to move.

items.title: Hospitality body's donations to Liberals questioned
items.description: The Tasmanian Greens have accused the state's peak hospitality group and the Liberal Party of a "political stitch-up" to kill off the proposed mandatory pokies card, after hundreds of thousands of dollars in donations were revealed.
